citation: Smith and Bazant (2017). Multiphase Porous Electrode Theory. Journal of the Electrochemical Society 164, E3291-E3310. https://doi.org/10.1149/2.0171711jes
description: MPET is the TRI-AMDD group's porous-electrode simulation software for rechargeable batteries. It resolves coupled electrolyte and active-material dynamics, including phase separation in electrode materials, using a volume-averaged multiscale formulation. Inputs specify physical parameters and imposed current or voltage protocols; outputs include internal concentrations, potentials and reaction rates together with terminal current and voltage. It represents a battery cell or electrode, not a grid-scale storage fleet. Spatial and temporal detail depend on the configured discretisation and cycling protocol. The LICENSE starts with MIT terms and adds academic citation conditions; source is free, and the repository documents installation and result analysis. Temperature dependence is identified as missing from the comparison with dualfoil. That limit matters for thermal-management or safety studies. MPET can help generate battery performance assumptions for electricity-storage simulations. The methods paper describes the theory, but no battery case was run during this metadata review.
